text:
Good morning. It is Wednesday, November eleventh. 

First, the news from home.

Story one. In parliament, lawmakers have rescinded the passage of the Anti-L G B T Q Plus Bill to correct inconsistencies in the legislation. Three News reports that the motion to withdraw the passed bill was moved on Monday by the Majority Leader, James Agalga. 

Story two. A heated contest is building within the opposition New Patriotic Party ahead of the twenty twenty-eight elections, with several high-profile figures declaring bids for parliamentary primaries. Both Joy Online and Three News report that former Deputy Director of Communications at the Presidency, Jefferson Sackey, is running for Ablekuma Central, while former President John Agyekum Kufuor's son, Edward Agyekum Kufuor, is contesting Atwima Nwabiagya North, alongside bids from former youth leader Akosua Manu and musician Obour.

Story three. The Speaker of Parliament, Alban Sumana Kingsford Bagbin, has directed that plenary sittings will now strictly begin at two o'clock in the afternoon on sitting days. Graphic Online reports that mornings will now be reserved for committee work to improve punctuality and establish a predictable schedule for members.

Story four. The Chairman of the African Political Parties Initiative, Johnson Asiedu Nketiah, has urged political organisations across Africa to focus on building the capacity to govern rather than just chasing election victories. Joy Online reports that the N D C stalwart emphasised that parties need institutional strength and technical expertise to deliver for their citizens once in power.

Now, around the world.

Story five. United States and Ukrainian officials are holding a second day of American-mediated security talks with Russia in Abu Dhabi. France Twenty-Four reports that Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky expressed satisfaction with the evolving diplomatic approach as Washington pushes for a new security framework.

Story six. In the United States, hardline conservative and Donald Trump ally Jim Jordan has been elected as the leader of the House Republicans following their recent midterm election defeat. France Twenty-Four reports that Jordan defeated Steve Scalise in a secret ballot and will now lead the party in opposition after Republicans lost control of both chambers of Congress.

You can open Dad News and ask for more about any story by its number.
